The Spring Ledger is a long-form fantasy Series exploring a shared water commons, the institutions that govern it, the meanings attached to obligation, and the consequences of changing collective practices. Its identity should preserve wonder, discovery, everyday belonging, meaningful relationships, institutional transformation, material consequences, and the possibility of hopeful flourishing. Do not turn it into a generic escalating-villain epic.

Experience brief: Wonder, discovery, meaningful adventure, everyday belonging, emotionally consequential relationships and an ultimately hopeful possibility of flourishing. Author-fixed experience brief; working and noncanonical.

Ysa Trant and the maintenance lineages: the Right is conditional on training, so they need the condition demonstrated or the Right is exposed. They guard craft standards and fear dilution by untrained gift-hands. Their stake in the review is an agent inference.

The cohort's belief is no longer uniform. The Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation, so plurality of practice now crosses generations as well as communities.

Book 24 is where the Long Return's labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule. A generation that refuses to be counted is asked to give back the water before it is owed. The Book exercises the Old Hand, the Ledger and the Source, and exports one new kind of record: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance, that says who can repair rather than who
A generation that came of age after Book 20 has never seen the labour, because lineage crews perform it under the Right.
The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage. Its review point falls in Book 24 (agent-proposed as P1; the source gives a reversal for it).
The cohort, now practising both counted and uncounted return, may claim standing in how the valley coordinates its channel work. Book 24 names no body that would grant that standing and creates none.

trajectory.development: Book 24 has a generation that came of age after Book 20 and has never seen the labour, because lineage crews perform it under the Right. The Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within that one generation.

trajectory.changes: Makes plural practice a matter across generations as well as communities, as E4 states. E4 is attributed unknown_legacy, so the provenance of the split is not established.

trajectory.development: Book 24 is where the labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule, and the Special Draw Right's review point falls in Book 24. Both placements are agent-proposed (E5, E7).
